title: HIV Antibody ELISA Kit Protocol
author: Devi Oktafiani
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7gyhjxw

steps.title: Prepare plasma samples
steps.instruction: Collect 3 mL whole blood from a plain (red‑cap) tube, then centrifuge at approximately 1000 × g for 15 min to obtain plasma.

steps.title: Dilute wash buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare 20‑fold diluted wash buffer by adding 25 mL concentrated wash buffer to 475 mL distilled water (final volume 500 mL).

steps.title: Equilibrate reagents to RT
steps.instruction: Allow all kit components and samples to reach room temperature for at least 30 min before use.

steps.title: Select and store unused strips
steps.instruction: Determine the number of wells required; keep any unused strips dry and store them at 4 °C.

steps.title: Add controls and samples
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of Negative Control to three wells, 50 µL of HIV‑1 Positive Control to one well, 50 µL of HIV‑2 Positive Control to another well, and leave one well blank (no solution). Add 50 µL of each plasma sample to its designated well. Dispense the liquid at the bottom of each well without touching the side walls, then gently shake the plate to mix.

steps.title: Incubate first binding step
steps.instruction: Seal the plate with a cover and incubate at 37 °C for 60 min.

steps.title: Discard unbound material
steps.instruction: Remove the cover and discard the well contents by tapping the plate onto absorbent filter paper or another absorbent material.

steps.title: Wash plate after first incubation
steps.instruction: Wash the plate five times with the diluted wash buffer, ensuring wells never dry completely.

substeps.instruction: Discard the previous solution without touching side walls.
Fill each well completely with wash buffer.
Incubate on an ELISA shaker for 2 min.
Invert the plate, decant the buffer, and tap 4–5 times on absorbent paper towel to remove residual liquid.
Repeat the above wash cycle a total of five times.

steps.title: Add HRP‑conjugate
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of HRP‑conjugate working solution to every well except the blank, dispensing at the bottom without touching side walls.

steps.title: Incubate HRP reaction
steps.instruction: Seal the plate and incubate at 37 °C for 30 min.

steps.title: Wash plate after HRP
steps.instruction: Wash the plate five times with wash buffer, avoiding complete drying of wells.

substeps.instruction: Discard solution without contacting side walls.
Fill wells with wash buffer, shake 2 min on ELISA shaker.
Invert, decant, and tap 4–5 times on absorbent paper.
Repeat for a total of five washes.

steps.title: Add TMB substrate
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of TMB substrate A and 50 µL of TMB substrate B to each well. Cover the plate and incubate at 37 °C in the dark for 15–20 min (do not exceed 30 min). Stop incubation when a visible gradient appears in the positive‑control wells.

steps.title: Add stop solution
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL of Stop solution to every well, including the blank. A color change to yellow should occur; gently tap the plate to ensure thorough mixing.

steps.title: Read plate absorbance
steps.instruction: Verify that the plate bottom is free of fingerprints, water, and bubbles. Measure absorbance at 450 nm immediately.

steps.title: Calculate results and interpret
steps.instruction: Compute mean absorbance of positive controls (must be ≥ 0.80) and negative controls (must be ≤ 0.08). Determine the cut‑off: if negative control < 0.05, cut‑off = 0.05 + 0.10 = 0.15; if negative control ≥ 0.05, cut‑off = negative control + 0.10. The assay is valid only if the control criteria are met. Classify each sample as negative when its OD < cut‑off and positive when its OD ≥ cut‑off.
